question: Does the 2011 Marikina River DNA-barcode study independently resolve its reported Pterygoplichthys specimens to P. pardalis and P. disjunctivus for species-level projection?
citation: Jumawan, J. C., Vallejo, B. M., Herrera, A. A., Buerano, C. C., & Fontanilla, I. K. C. (2011). DNA barcodes of the suckermouth sailfin catfish Pterygoplichthys (Siluriformes: Loricariidae) in the Marikina River system, Philippines: Molecular perspective of an invasive alien fish species. Philippine Science Letters, 4(2), 103-113. Published 2011-12-09.

sourceAccess.accessMethod: Reviewed the full journal-hosted article text and its methods, results, discussion, voucher, and sequence-accession statements on 2026-11-19. UP Diliman's faculty publication page confirms the article citation; the journal archive lists the issue and starting page.
sourceAccess.licenseFinding: No item-specific open license or permission to reuse the paper's text, figures, specimen images, or sequence-derived graphics was identified. No figures or sequence files were copied.

fieldSampling.samplingDate: Not stated in the reviewed article text.
fieldSampling.stationLimit: The article does not give coordinates or assign individual sample counts, dates, or sequence identifiers to each Marikina station. Its Figure 1 was not digitized or reused.
fieldSampling.voucherClaim: The article says its specimens were deposited at the Zoological Museum, Institute of Biology, UP Diliman, under morphology-category labels P0 1-6, P1 1-6, P2 1-6, P3 1-6, P4 1-6, and P5 1-6. The physical vouchers were not independently inspected in this review.
fieldSampling.separateMindanaoComparison: The paper also used seven specimens from Agusan Marsh, Mindanao, as a geographic comparison. Those samples are outside this NCR review and are not assigned to Marikina or treated as a Mindanao species checklist.

sourceMorphologyCategories.preidentifiedDescription: Intergrade abdominal patterns in the P. pardalis range

taxonomicFindings.molecularMethod: A 655-base-pair mitochondrial COI fragment was amplified for all 36 Marikina specimens.
resultsAsReported: Six COI haplotypes were identified in the 36 Marikina specimens.
The paper reports low divergence and shared genealogy that did not consistently match the morphology-based categories.
Twenty-eight of the 30 P0-P4 specimens shared haplotype H1; among the six P5 specimens, four shared H6 and two shared H1.
The authors report that BOLD species-level matches were conflicting and did not accurately identify their Pterygoplichthys sequences.

The authors discuss possible introgressive hybridization but also state that one variable species and incomplete lineage sorting cannot be excluded; they note a lack of suitable reference barcodes and call for nuclear-gene work.
taxonomicFindings.interpretation: This is direct, voucher-linked genus-level Marikina evidence, but it does not independently resolve the sampled fish into two species. The article's P. pardalis and P. disjunctivus terms describe morphology-based pre-identifications and comparator sequences amid explicit species-boundary uncertainty.

evidenceDecision.decision: Retain the study as strong historical, site-named Pterygoplichthys genus-level evidence and as a species-identity caution. Do not add two verified species rows.
evidenceDecision.reason: The article identifies the specimens as Pterygoplichthys and documents vouchers and sequence ranges, but the authors report weak COI separation, discordant morphology, conflicting database matches, incomplete reference coverage, and unresolved hybridization/single-species alternatives. Station-level specimen mapping and collection dates were not recovered.

nonClaims: Morphology-based labels are not treated as independently confirmed species identifications.
The 36 specimens cannot be distributed evenly or otherwise apportioned among the five stations from the reviewed article.
The seven Agusan Marsh comparison specimens do not create a Mindanao checklist or validate continuity between Agusan Marsh and Marikina River.
The study does not establish present-day abundance, current presence at every named station, fishing access, legal catchability, safety, or diet guidance.
The article's title and invasion framing are not independently adopted as a species-specific status decision.
nextActions: Reconcile the reported Marikina GenBank accessions JF498719-JF498754 and BOLD process IDs BMP001-11 through BMP036-11 against their public metadata and the article's museum-voucher labels; retain any missing or ambiguous station fields.
Check whether the Zoological Museum can provide a catalog crosswalk from P0-P5 voucher labels to individual collection events without assuming access or reuse permission.

Keep the earlier 2023 Marikina host-fish crosswalk's two reported Pterygoplichthys names as source-reported candidates, not as molecularly verified species records; continue NCR habitat and species-source work.
